subject: Term-shift opportunity: usage -> quality convergence & ROI snapshot
messages:
From: Dana Park <dana@lumenai.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q3 usage snapshot + term options

Hi Grace / Ben / Karthik,

Attaching Q3 usage and a small sample of latency traces (perf_samples_aug.zip). We've seen a steady 2.6x increase in token spend month-over-month as we roll out the new summarization feature; most of the growth is in embeddings and short-chat generation. A few notes: 

- Token mix: 65% embeddings, 25% chat, 10% reranking.
- Latency: p95 for chat has crept from 210ms to ~320ms over peak hours (attached traces).
- Business signal: higher conversion on personalized summaries — strong ROI on user engagement but budget runway is short.

We are evaluating a term shift from trial / month-to-month into a 6–12 month reserved commitment. Two asks before our exec procurement call next Tues:
1) A short ROI sketch that maps their current run-rate to commit tiers (monthly token burn -> committed tokens -> unit price).
2) Any performance guarantees or fallbacks if we hit latency regressions with our heavier KV cache use.

Can you confirm what a staggered commit would look like (e.g., 3mo ramp -> steady commit) and whether we can get a short burst credit for the initial migration?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

Best,
Dana
Dana Park
Head of Platform Engineering, LumenAI
Dana@lumenai.com

Attachments: lumenai_usage_Q3_2027.csv (csv), perf_samples_aug.zip (zip)

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Dana Park <dana@lumenai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 usage snapshot + term options

Dana — thanks for the data, this is helpful context. Quick read-through and initial thoughts below.

Summary snapshot (attached): redwood_snapshot_pre-read.pdf — 2 slides: 1) Cost to commit mapping, 2) p95 impact scenarios and recommended guardrails.

Observations:
- Embeddings-heavy workloads are an ideal candidate for reserved capacity + dynamic quantization; we can show ~28–35% token-cost reduction with our suggested quantization profile for the embeddings model.
- The jump in chat p95 looks correlated with peak concurrency; we suggest enabling KV-prefetch + a small increase in dedicated allocation during a 4–6 week ramp.

Proposed next steps (suggested MAP):
1) 6-month staged commit: Month 1-2 at 60% expected run-rate (to limit upfront spend), Month 3-6 at 100% with an evaluation at end of Month 4.
2) One-time 15% burst credit on the first month to offset migration cost — conditional on a signed 6-month paid commit.
3) SLAs: we can commit to p95 latency targets per-route with automatic fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant if regressions >15% over baseline; we'll include tracing hooks so your SREs can alert quicker.

I'll let Ben add the economics and Karthik add operational constraints, but we can prep a 30-min pre-read review for your procurement call. 

If that sounds reasonable, can we pencil in Tue 8/24 10:00am PT for a 30-min sync?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_snapshot_pre-read.pdf

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-20T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 usage snapshot + term options (pricing & credits)

Grace / Karthik — adding pricing structure and the customer-facing wording for the MAP. Key points: 

- Pricing: 3-tier commit model for LumenAI based on observed run-rate:
  * Tier A: 1.2M tokens/month -> $0.0009/token
  * Tier B: 3.5M tokens/month -> $0.00075/token
  * Tier C: 8M tokens/month -> $0.00062/token

- Proposed offer: 6-month staged commit (as Grace outlined) + a one-time 15% burst credit applied to Month 1 invoice. If they sign a 12-month firm commit we can improve to 18% burst credit and a 3% invoice-level discount after Month 6.

- Operational caveats: we need a short SLA appendix that clarifies fallback to a compatible model variant when p95 regressions >15% and a joint runbook for debugging KV cache-induced slowdowns.

I've created a preliminary HubSpot deal note (see link) and an internal ops ticket template we can attach to the MAP.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
